note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: Gallery panel 7 (index 6) is Cody Stricker's REAL rooted same-species plant: fine pale fibrous roots emerge from the basal sheaths and living green culms. This clears the ROOT ATTACHMENT evidence role. But the published shallow cormlike base (approximately 5×3 mm) is NOT cleanly exposed or measurable in these pixels; panel 6 (index 5), though in the SAME research-grade iNaturalist observation, does not prove physically continuous flowering culm to the rooted base. Use exact vouchered one-individual macro to establish actual corm size. Bob Harms index 7 shows aerial culms and flowering panicles, but no connected root.
tiles.short: Actual fibrous roots photographed; cormlike swelling still unmeasured
tiles.status: ACTUAL ROOTS AND BASAL SHOOTS PHOTOGRAPHED — DISTINCT CORM AND FLOWERING LINK STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 02 · OPEN THE TRUE COLLAR
tiles.details: Index 11 (panel 12) is actual Bob Harms source photo showing green blade–sheath junctions with clearly visible LONG blade-margin hairs. They do NOT substitute for the dense short (0.25–0.5 mm) FREE INNER ligule hairs reported in Williamson County treatment. Cody rooted habit (index 6) provides sheaths only, no opening of a true collar at microscope scale. A 1-mm physical bar and view from INSIDE the opened sheath are needed before a diagnostic hair-fringe arrow is placed.
tiles.status: TRUE COLLAR LOCATION AND LONG MARGIN HAIRS SHOWN — SHORT INNER LIGULE NOT PROVED

tiles.heading: 03 · FOLLOW LEAVES TO PANICLE
tiles.details: Bob Harms index 7 displays flowering leafy culms and entire small open panicles; index 8 shows multiple same-species panicle branches. Cody index 5 has a very useful bright green close flowering panicle against a hand with one true narrow leaf blade. Original iNat index 0 is another source-identified attached small spikelet/pedicel view. Never infer corm-to-panicle connection from separate photos without same-individual matching.
tiles.short: Narrow stem blades, open spring panicle
tiles.status: GROSS ATTACHED CULM AND PANICLE COVERED

tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE MATURE SPIKELETS
tiles.details: Harms index 9 has a photographed scale beside actual obovoid spikelets on slender stalks, and index 10 provides flowering reproductive closer detail. Cody index 5 confirms similarly green attached spikelets, but hands/fingers are not 1-mm scientific rulers. Published mature length 3–3.5 mm and width 1.3–1.8 mm remain reported source ranges; the archival scale is useful but no individually isolated ripe spikelet has been calibrated and dissected here.
tiles.status: ACTUAL SCALED PANICLE/SPIKELET PLATE — ISOLATED MEASURED RIPE SPIKELET STILL NEEDED

tiles.heading: 05 · SEPARATE GLUMES AND LEMMAS
tiles.details: Bob Harms indexes 9–10 show true source-labelled attached spikelets and scale, not separate glumes. Published lower glume about 1.5–2.1 mm, upper 2.5–2.8 mm; sterile lower and bisexual fertile upper florets lie WITHIN one complete spikelet. DO NOT arrow an unresolved glossy green margin as a measured glume/lemma or call a projecting flower organ an awn.
tiles.short: Lower/upper glumes and two florets: calibration and dissection still missing
tiles.status: UNSEPARATED ORIGINAL SPIKELETS COVERED — GROSS DISSECTION STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 06 · COMPARE CORM-BASED PANICGRASS AND ITS LOOK-ALIKES
tiles.details: Three separately identified DIFFERENT species are panels 3–5 (indices 2–4): D. commutatum macro, D. lindheimeri scene, D. oligosanthes panicle. Exact D. pedicellatum own-source reproductive panels 6 and 10 (indices 5,9) and rooted crown index 6 help contrast the corm-based growth habit. Do not compare spikelet sizes from unscaled photos: *D. oligosanthes* overlaps 3–3.5 mm; actual root morphology and free inner ligule size needed. Two Cody Stricker photographs now stored in this CORRECT species card, not Lindheimer.
tiles.short: Overlaps oligosanthes: use collar AND base
tiles.status: THREE CORRECT LOOK-ALIKES + ROOT AND FLOWER PHOTO LESSONS — MATCHED-SCALE DIFFERENCES MISSING

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: CORM-BASED PANICGRASS (*Dichanthelium pedicellatum*): SEE ACTUAL attached fibrous roots and basal leaves in gallery panel 7 (Cody Stricker), with a source-connected but separate small green flowering spikelet panicle in panel 6 and fully leafy flowering stems in Bob Harms panels 8–9. The true cormlike swelling (~5×3 mm) is NOT clearly isolated on a measured same-plant root photo, and the SHORT 0.25–0.5 mm inner HAIR CURTAIN ligule is NOT the long, externally visible blade-edge cilia on Harms panel 12. Spindle/obovoid ripe spikelets ~3–3.5 mm, with two unequal glumes, require individual ruler-calibrated dissection for species-grade ID. THIS is not a winter basal-rosette grass. Do not misfile Cody photos as D. lindheimeri.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: START source-photo gallery panel 7 (index 6), Cody Stricker: Actual fibrous roots attached directly below living basal shoots. The tiny cormlike bulge is still not isolated with a 1mm ruler; never annotate one by inference.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Index 11 (panel 12) is actual Bob Harms source photo showing green blade–sheath junctions with clearly visible LONG blade-margin hairs. They do NOT substitute for the dense short (0.25–0.5 mm) FREE INNER ligule hairs reported in Williamson County treatment. Cody rooted habit (index 6) provides sheaths only, no opening of a true collar at microscope scale. A 1-mm physical bar and view from INSIDE the opened sheath are needed before a diagnostic hair-fringe arrow is placed.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Bob Harms index 7 displays flowering leafy culms and entire small open panicles; index 8 shows multiple same-species panicle branches. Cody index 5 has a very useful bright green close flowering panicle against a hand with one true narrow leaf blade. Original iNat index 0 is another source-identified attached small spikelet/pedicel view. Never infer corm-to-panicle connection from separate photos without same-individual matching.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Versus D. oligosanthes, 3–3.5 mm spikelet size overlaps; focus on genuinely narrow thin culm blades and a ~0.25–0.5 mm true collar hair fringe against oligosanthes' often longer 1–4 mm fringe. Lindheimer has tiny 1.3–1.6 mm spikelets; commutatum has broader often cordate stem blades and minute/absent ligule. Hair fringe must be viewed at scale, not inferred from isolated panicles.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: TRUE COLLAR LOCATION — visible blade/sheath insertion and nearby hairs (NOT inner ligule)
panels.caption: Jared Shorma's exact-species Garner State Park photo truly shows a leaf blade joining its green sheath, small pale hairs at the corner and a long overlapping green culm. The blade is NOT folded back to expose the inside, so a claimed 0.25–0.5 mm short inner fringe would be unjustified. No mm scale.

panels.label: GROWTH FORM — living flowering pedicellate panicgrass in rocky Texas
panels.caption: This research-grade Glen Rose plant photo by ashleyrsteel shows a crowded tuft of narrow living grass blades with small flowering panicles across limestone/rocky field habitat. It's a useful beginner full-habit photo, but multiple neighboring grasses can overlap and roots/corms remain concealed by soil.

panels.label: LOOK-ALIKE: Lindheimer panicgrass — genuine 1-mm-scaled tiny spikelets
panels.caption: This photograph is *Dichanthelium lindheimeri*, NOT *D. pedicellatum*. Dan Johnson's source photographs actual small, green-to-burgundy oval spikelets attached to threadlike pedicels with a genuine original 1.00-mm bar. The Texas botanical descriptions give mature spikelets about 1.3–1.7 mm in Lindheimer versus about 3–3.5 mm in pedicellate panicgrass. These are from DIFFERENT original photographers/camera scales: never estimate the pedicellate specimen's spikelet length directly from the other species' image. Measure your own with a ruler.

intro: CORM-BASED PANICGRASS (*Dichanthelium pedicellatum*): SEE ACTUAL attached fibrous roots and basal leaves in gallery panel 7 (Cody Stricker), with a source-connected but separate small green flowering spikelet panicle in panel 6 and fully leafy flowering stems in Bob Harms panels 8–9. The true cormlike swelling (~5×3 mm) is NOT clearly isolated on a measured same-plant root photo, and the SHORT 0.25–0.5 mm inner HAIR CURTAIN ligule is NOT the long, externally visible blade-edge cilia on Harms panel 12. Spindle/obovoid ripe spikelets ~3–3.5 mm, with two unequal glumes, require individual ruler-calibrated dissection for species-grade ID. THIS is not a winter basal-rosette grass. Do not misfile Cody photos as D. lindheimeri.
memory_rule: FIRST find the REAL fibrous-rooted base and look for a small cormlike swelling (not a basal rosette). SECOND show true INSIDE 0.25–0.5 mm HAIR FRINGE (not long blade-margin hairs). THIRD measure three ripe 3–3.5 mm obovoid spikelets. Lindheimer ~1.3–1.7, commutatum ~2.1–3.2, oligosanthes ~2.9–4 mm; substantial overlap needs morphology, not just numbers.
safety_note: 16 real physically archived species JPEGs, one historical illustration, 3 true different-species comparisons; 17 gallery panels including 5 new high-value selected Texas CC BY photos, 11 new visible-only arrows, no new fake sub-mm labels. Relevant *D. lindheimeri* comparator now genuine 1-mm CC BY spikelet macro rather than the previously ambiguous mixed-grass CC BY-NC source. Conservative six-role =4.5/6 (75%). Taxon source still does not prove Hays county voucher; Pages deployment pending.
field_rule: There is a crucial difference between a documented attached fibrous root system and a documented swollen subterranean corm; and between exterior collar hairs and the TRUE inner 0.25–0.5mm ligule. Verify with real scale.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
